paper_id: Targeted Backdoor Attacks on Deep Learning Systems Using Data Poisoning
evidence: We repeat the above experiment 10 times, and we observe that in all these 10 experiments, the attack success rate is 100%.
we perform the backdoor attacks against two state-of-theart face recognition models, which are DeepID [62] and VGG-Face [55] respectively.
We use the YouTube Aligned Face dataset for evaluation, which is a pre-processed dataset of images taken from the YouTube Faces dataset
Attack success rate is the percentage of backdoor instances classified as the target label.
unresolved: n_seeds=10 is the stated repetition count only for the input-instance-key repeat-trial experiment in Section V-A ('We repeat the above experiment 10 times'); the paper does not state a uniform repeat/seed protocol applied across all reported results (Blended Injection, Accessory Injection, Blended Accessory Injection results appear to be single runs per configuration).

n_baselines=0: this is a first-of-its-kind attack paper with no prior poisoning method re-implemented and compared numerically against the four proposed strategies (input-instance-key, Blended Injection, Accessory Injection, Blended Accessory Injection). Section VII separately evaluates three candidate DEFENSE strategies (label-distribution check, L2-distance outlier detector, auxiliary-pristine-data/VGG-Face) against the attacks -- these are defenses being stress-tested, not comparison baselines for the attack method, so they are not counted in n_baselines.

n_datasets=1: only the YouTube Aligned Face dataset is used; the 50 physically-photographed images in Section VI are additional test-time captures layered on top of the same dataset/labels, not a second dataset.

reports_variability='prose': variability is reported as narrative ranges (e.g., standard test accuracy 'vary from 97.50% to 97.85%' across the 10 repeated trials) rather than as an explicit table/figure of per-trial values, std, or CIs.
